question.problem:
Let $X$ and $Y$ be two continuous random variables with the joint probability density function

$$
f(x,y)=\{\begin{aligned}2y\operatorname{cos}⁡x, & \,0\le x\le \frac{\pi }{2},\,0\le y\le 1, \\ 0, & \,\text{otherwise}.\end{aligned}
$$

Find the expected value of $Y.$
question.worked_solution:
The marginal density function for $Y$ when $0\le y\le 1$ is 

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{Y}(y) & ={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }f(x,y)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}2y\operatorname{cos}⁡x\,\text{d}x \\  & =2y[\operatorname{sin}⁡x]_{0}^{\pi /2} \\  & =2y(\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})-\operatorname{sin}⁡0) \\  & =2y(1-0) \\  & =2y.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the full expression for ${f}_{X}(x)$ is given by

$$
{f}_{X}(x)=\{\begin{aligned}2y, & 0\le y\le 1, \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the  expected value of $Y$ is 

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[Y] & ={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }y\cdot {f}_{Y}(y)\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}y\cdot 2y\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}2{y}^{2}\,\text{d}y \\  & ={[\frac{2}{3}{y}^{3}]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =(\frac{2}{3}-0) \\  & =\frac{2}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$
